validity.recommendation: Merge/retire P2214 as a superseded duplicate of P6562 (Kanai Chhata-Panitar Gas Pipeline, status=construction). Do not count both rows' length/capacity in tracker totals -- there is only ONE PNGRB authorization (PNGRB/Auth/2-NGPL/BID/KSPL/(8)/2019, granted 08.07.2019 to Hooghly Pipelines Private Limited/HPPL, an H-Energy group SPV) behind both rows.
validity.researcher_notes: Started from the sheet's own wiki citations, all pngrb.gov.in. The PNGRB authorization number cited (PNGRB/Auth/2-NGPL/BID/KSPL/(8)/2019) is the SAME number printed on a 01-Aug-2022 PNGRB letter I downloaded and read directly (image-only scan, no text layer, so I rendered it to PNG and read it visually since url_verifier's substring check cannot parse scanned PDFs): 'Amendment in letter of Grant of Authorization for Kanai Chhata - Shrirampur Natural Gas pipeline due to shifting of termination point from Shrirampur to Panitar', addressed to HPPL director Abhirup Bhattacharya, approving the shift 'as per sub-regulation (3) of Regulation 13' and revising the authorized trunk length from 242 km to 266 km. I then pulled two PNGRB national-register PDFs at different dates and grepped the extracted text (pdftotext -layout): the 25-Jun-2021 register (pre-amendment) lists row 5.11.NGPL as 'Kanai Chhata - Shrirampur', sponsor HPPL, auth date 08.07.2019, 317 km, 19.20 (capacity), target 'July, 2022', West Bengal; the 26-Jun-2024 register (post-amendment) lists the SAME row number 5.11.NGPL, same sponsor HPPL, same auth date 08.07.2019, same 317 km, same 19.20 capacity, target 'March 2024', West Bengal -- but now named 'Kanai - Chhata - Panitar'. Every field (sponsor, authorization date, length, capacity, state) is identical across the two register vintages; only the pipeline's public name and terminus changed, via the confirmed regulatory amendment. GEM's own live sheet already carries this exact successor as P6562 (Kanai Chhata-Panitar Gas Pipeline, Status=construction, LengthKnown=317, Capacity=19.20, ProposalYear=2019, StartYear1=2024, LastUpdated=2025-07-17) -- an exact match to the 2024 PNGRB register row. So P2214 and P6562 are not two different projects; P2214 is the pre-2022-amendment name/config of the identical authorized pipeline that P6562 now tracks live. Keeping P2214 as a separate 'cancelled' 250 km/19.2 MMSCMD project double-counts against the one real 317 km authorization. This also resolves the orchestrator's flagged question about P6562 being a possible predecessor/sibling: it is the direct successor, same PID lineage split across two rows.

validity.recommendation: Correct EndState/Province from 'Maharashtra' to 'West Bengal' (Shrirampur is a village in Nadia district, West Bengal -- not the Shrirampur in Ahmednagar district, Maharashtra). This is very likely a place-name collision error, not a real cross-country route: a 250 km pipeline cannot plausibly run from coastal West Bengal to Maharashtra (>1,500 km apart), and every PNGRB source below places the entire route inside West Bengal.
validity.researcher_notes: PNGRB's own bidding-round route map for this exact project (https://www.pngrb.gov.in/pdf/ngp/bid/bid12/Map-KSPL-Bidding.pdf) has an embedded text layer I extracted with pdftotext (url_verifier's substring check can't reach it either -- confirmed manually): 'KANAI CHATTA - SHRIRAMPUR NATURAL GAS PIPELINE ... Directions from Kanai Chatta, West Bengal to Shrirampur, Nadia, West Bengal' via Nandakumar and Kolaghat, both West Bengal. Both the 2021 and 2024 PNGRB national registers (cited under the duplicate finding above) also list the State column as 'West Bengal' for this exact authorization. GEM's own EndState/Province='Maharashtra' is contradicted by all three independent PNGRB documents (a route map, and two register editions years apart).

fills.researcher_notes: Neither document uses the word 'cancelled' (PNGRB's vocabulary is 'amendment'/'shifting of termination point'), so contains_value is false for both -- but together they are dispositive that the named 'Kanai Chhata-Shrirampur' project, at this endpoint, will never be built: PNGRB formally approved moving the terminus to Panitar in 2022, and by the 2024 national register the 'Shrirampur' name has vanished entirely, replaced by 'Kanai - Chhata - Panitar' at the same register line. See the duplicate concern -- this is a CONFIRMED supersession, which is the strongest form of 'cancelled' for this exact route/name, even though the underlying authorization lives on as P6562.
PNGRB's register is titled 'Natural Gas Pipeline Networks in India' and lists this row under its Natural Gas Pipeline (NGPL) framework -- unambiguously a gas pipeline.

The amendment letter explicitly discusses 'the total length of the trunk pipeline' and authorizes it under PNGRB's NGPL common-carrier trunk-pipeline regulations (Regulation 13(3)) -- a transmission trunk line, not a gathering/distribution/CGD network.

PNGRB's authorization number itself is 'PNGRB/Auth/2-NGPL/BID/KSPL/(8)/2019' and both registers list the authorization date as 08.07.2019, matching GEM's ProposalYear=2019 (used here as the grant/authorization year; the underlying bid round, per the PNGRB bid-page reference 'BID/NGPL/12/2018/02/KSPL/01', ran in 2018, but 2019 -- the year the authorization was actually granted -- is the better-evidenced and defensible year).

Could not source 2023. PNGRB's 2021 register (pre-amendment, under the Shrirampur name) gives a target completion of 'July, 2022'; its 2024 register (post-amendment, under the Panitar name -- i.e. GEM's own P6562, which already carries StartYear1=2024) gives 'March 2024'. Neither PNGRB vintage supports 2023. Given the row is superseded (see duplicate finding), recommend dropping StartYear1 rather than sourcing it to a figure that matches neither PNGRB target date.

Exact match, '19.20', in BOTH the 2021 and 2024 PNGRB national registers, three years apart and under both the pre- and post-amendment names -- capacity was unaffected by the 2022 terminus shift. Strongest-sourced value on this row.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=cancelled is right for THIS exact named route, but it is currently unsourced (blank ShelvedCancelledType, one of the 8 flagged blanks in this cluster) and the reason recorded should be precise. This is not a dormancy inference -- it is a CONFIRMED regulatory supersession: a 01-Aug-2022 PNGRB letter (read directly; scanned image, no OCR text layer, so verified visually rather than by substring match) approved HPPL's request to shift the pipeline's termination point from Shrirampur to Panitar under the same authorization number (PNGRB/Auth/2-NGPL/BID/KSPL/(8)/2019). By PNGRB's 26-Jun-2024 national register, the 'Shrirampur' name has disappeared entirely from the authorized-pipelines list and the identical register line (same sponsor HPPL, same 08.07.2019 authorization date, same 317 km, same 19.20 MMSCMD capacity) now reads 'Kanai - Chhata - Panitar' -- exactly matching GEM's own P6562 (Kanai Chhata-Panitar Gas Pipeline, Status=construction). So the Shrirampur-named project is confirmed dead as such, superseded by a formal regulatory amendment, not merely gone quiet. Recommend ShelvedCancelledType=confirmed and CancelledYear=2022 (the amendment-letter date, the clearest dated point at which this specific route ceased to be the authorized configuration). IMPORTANT CAVEAT, tied to the duplicate finding in validity: the underlying pipeline is not actually dead -- it is under active construction today as P6562. The 'cancelled' label here should be understood, and ideally handled by a merge/retirement of this row (see validity), rather than left standing as an independent cancelled 250 km/19.2 MMSCMD project alongside the live 317 km/19.2 MMSCMD P6562, which double-counts one authorization as two projects.

summary: P2214 is a confirmed-cancelled/superseded duplicate of P6562 -- same PNGRB authorization (08.07.2019, HPPL/H-Energy SPV) renamed Shrirampur->Panitar by a 01-Aug-2022 amendment and now tracked live as P6562 (construction, 317 km, 19.20 MMSCMD) -- plus two independent GEM data errors on P2214 itself: EndState/Province should be West Bengal not Maharashtra, and LengthKnown should be ~317 km not 250 (both contradicted by PNGRB's own route map and two register editions three years apart); Fuel/PipelineType/Capacity/ProposalYear now sourced, StartYear1=2023 and Owner1=H-Energy left UNRESOLVED (no PNGRB or verifiable source supports 2023, and henergy.com fails TLS verification).
